Conclusion: The test `tests.test_utils_datatypes.LocalCacheTest.test_cache_without_limit(self)` checks whether the `LocalCache` class can handle a large number of items without setting a limit. However, the test failure indicates that the `__init__` method of the `LocalCache` class does not initialize the `limit` attribute correctly, leading to a `TypeError` when trying to compare it with the length of the cache in the `__setitem__` method.

The issue arises because the `__init__` method of `LocalCache` accepts an optional `limit` parameter, but it is not properly initialized if no value is provided. As a result, when the `test_cache_without_limit` method tries to compare the length of the cache with the `limit`, it encounters a `TypeError` because it is trying to compare an integer with `None`.

The best location to fix this issue is:

```
scrapy.utils.datatypes.LocalCache.__init__(self, limit=None)
```
